tools.name: wait
tools.description: Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.

parameters.name: cell_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

parameters.name: max_tokens
parameters.description: Output token budget for the wait call.

parameters.name: terminate
parameters.description: True stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.

parameters.name: yield_time_ms
parameters.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

parameters.name: questions
parameters.type: Array<{ header: string; id: string; options: Array<{ description: string; label: string; }>; question: string; }>
parameters.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

tools.name: exec
tools.description: Run JavaScript code to orchestrate/compose tool calls

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: JavaScript source text to execute. This tool only accepts string inputs that obey the lark grammar.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

parameters.name: path_prefix
parameters.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Relative or canonical task name (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description: Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.

parameters.name: fork_turns
parameters.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

parameters.name: reasoning_effort
parameters.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

parameters.name: task_name
parameters.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

parameters.name: timeout_ms
parameters.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: js
tools.description: UI automation through cua_repl using the initialized cua API.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: JavaScript to execute using the initialized cua_repl runtime.

parameters.name: timeout_ms
parameters.description: Optional execution timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000 (30 seconds) when omitted.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Short user-facing description of what this code block is doing. Prefer a few words in present-progressive form, such as 'Checking the mobile layout' or 'Comparing prices', over imperative or past-tense titles.

tools.name: js_reset
tools.description: Reset the persistent cua_repl JavaScript session. All JavaScript bindings are discarded. The next cua_repl.js call initializes a fresh runtime for the enabled surfaces. This does not close browser tabs or native apps, or erase their state. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

tools.name: apply_patch
tools.description: The `apply_patch` tool can be used to edit files. This is a FREEFORM tool, so do not wrap the patch in JSON.

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: unknown

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create a goal only when explicitly requested by the user or system/developer instructions; do not infer goals from ordinary tasks.

parameters.name: objective
parameters.description: The concrete objective to start pursuing. This starts a new active goal when no goal exists or replaces the current goal when it is complete.

parameters.name: token_budget
parameters.description: Positive token budget for the new goal. Omit unless explicitly requested.

tools.name: exec_command
tools.description: Runs a command in a PTY, returning output or a session ID for ongoing interaction.

parameters.name: cmd
parameters.description: Shell command to execute.

parameters.name: justification
parameters.description: User-facing approval question for `require_escalated`; omit otherwise.

parameters.name: login
parameters.description: Request login-shell startup. Omit to inherit.

parameters.name: max_output_tokens
parameters.description: Output token budget. Defaults to 10000 tokens; larger requests may be capped by policy.

parameters.name: prefix_rule
parameters.description: Reusable approval prefix for `cmd`, only with `sandbox_permissions: "require_escalated"`; for example ["git", "pull"].

parameters.name: sandbox_permissions
parameters.description: Per-command sandbox override. Defaults to `use_default`; use `require_escalated` for unsandboxed execution.

parameters.name: shell
parameters.description: Shell binary to launch. Defaults to the user's default shell.

parameters.name: tty
parameters.description: True allocates a PTY for the command; false or omitted uses plain pipes.

parameters.name: workdir
parameters.description: Working directory for the command. Defaults to the turn cwd.

parameters.name: yield_time_ms
parameters.description: Wait before yielding output. Defaults to 10000 ms; effective range is 250-30000 ms.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Get the current goal for this thread, including status, budgets, token and elapsed-time usage, and remaining token budget.

parameters.name: cursor

parameters.name: server

tools.description: Lists resources provided by MCP servers. Resources allow servers to share data that can be used by language models.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resources call; omit for the first page.

parameters.name: server
parameters.description: MCP server name. Omit to list resources from every configured server.

tools.name: read_mcp_resource
tools.description: Read a specific resource from an MCP server given the server name and resource URI.

parameters.name: server
parameters.description: MCP server name exactly as configured. Must match the 'server' field returned by list_mcp_resources.

parameters.name: uri
parameters.description: Resource URI to read. Must be one of the URIs returned by list_mcp_resources.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the existing goal.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Set status to `paused` only at the user's explicit request to pause this goal, never on your own initiative. Ask if unclear; a later resume revokes that request. Report the returned status and stop goal work. Budget limits take precedence over pausing. Set status to `complete` only when the objective has actually been achieved and no required work remains. Set status to `blocked` only when the same blocking condition has repeated for at least three consecutive goal turns, counting the original/user-triggered turn and any automatic continuations, and the agent cannot make meaningful progress without user input or an external-state change. If the user resumes a goal that was previously marked `blocked`, treat the resumed run as a fresh blocked audit. If the same blocking condition then repeats for at least three consecutive resumed goal turns, set status to `blocked` again. Once the blocked threshold is satisfied, do not keep reporting that you are still blocked while leaving the goal active; set status to `blocked`. Do not use `blocked` merely because the work is hard, slow, uncertain, incomplete, or would benefit from clarification. Do not mark a goal complete merely because its budget is nearly exhausted or because you are stopping work. You cannot use this tool to resume, budget-limit, or usage-limit a goal; those status changes are controlled by the user.

parameters.name: chars

parameters.name: max_output_tokens
parameters.description: Output token budget. Defaults to 10000 tokens; larger requests may be capped by policy.

parameters.name: session_id

parameters.name: yield_time_ms
parameters.description: Wait before yielding output. Non-empty writes default to 250 ms and cap at 30000 ms; empty polls wait 5000-300000 ms by default.
